title: Hilbert-Pluecker embedding and PGL linearization in arbitrary characteristic
statement: Let $k$ be any field [def-weil-field], $r\geq2$, and let $P$ be an admissible Hilbert polynomial, meaning the Hilbert polynomial of some closed subscheme of $\mathbf P^{r-1}$ over a field. Let $H=\operatorname{Hilb}^{P}(\mathbf P^{r-1}_k)$ be the scheme of [lem-sfb-projective-hilbert-polynomial-representability], with universal family $f:\mathcal X\to H$ and hyperplane line $L=\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}(1)$. There is an integer $M(P,r)$, independent of $k$, such that for every $m\geq M(P,r)$ the module $f_*L^{\otimes m}$ is locally free of rank $P(m)$, commutes with arbitrary base change, and is a quotient of the constant module $\operatorname{Sym}^m(k^r)\otimes_k\mathcal O_H$. The resulting morphism to the quotient Grassmannian of [lem-sfb-free-quotient-grassmann-projective], followed by its Pluecker map, is a closed immersion. Its hyperplane line is $\Lambda_m=\det(f_*L^{\otimes m})$. Changing projective coordinates defines an action of the group scheme $\operatorname{PGL}_{r,k}$, the group of invertible matrices modulo scalar matrices; the natural $\operatorname{SL}_{r,k}$ action linearizes $\Lambda_m$. The line $A_m=\Lambda_m^{\otimes r}$ has a $\operatorname{PGL}_{r,k}$-linearization whose pullback along $\operatorname{SL}_{r,k}\to\operatorname{PGL}_{r,k}$ is the induced linearization on that power. A linearization means a group-scheme action on the total line, linear on fibres and lifting the action on its base. Geometric semistable and stable loci for $(\operatorname{SL}_r,\Lambda_m)$ equal those for $(\operatorname{PGL}_r,A_m)$; these loci commute with field extension. Here, for either group acting on a projective scheme with a linearized ample line, a geometric point is semistable when an invariant section of some positive power is nonzero there, and stable when its orbit is closed in the semistable locus and its scheme-theoretic stabilizer has dimension zero. The corresponding loci are open subschemes. These statements hold in every characteristic, including when the central kernel $\mu_r=\operatorname{Spec}k[t]/(t^r-1)$ is nonreduced. The scheme, invertible-module, projective and ample conventions are [def-pc-scheme, def-sc-invertible-module, def-kun-projective, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module].

source.place: Section 2.1, printed pp.4--5, Hilbert embedding and determinant line; agent expansion of descent through the central group scheme mu_r, including nonreduced mu_r. Local PDF WANTED; read online at https://arxiv.org/pdf/0810.2340.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-hilbert-uniform-section-bound] with $n=r-1$ and polynomial $P$ to the universal closed family over $H$ furnished by [lem-sfb-projective-hilbert-polynomial-representability]. It is flat and finitely presented, and every geometric fibre has polynomial $P$, exactly the hypotheses of the bound. Choose its integer $b\geq1$ and set $M(P,r)=b$. For every $m\geq b$ we obtain the base-change-compatible exact sequence $0\to I_m\to V_m\otimes_k\mathcal O_H\to Q_m\to0$, with $V_m=\operatorname{Sym}^m(k^r)$, $Q_m=f_*L^{\otimes m}$ locally free of rank $P(m)$, and $I_m=p_*\mathcal I(m)$. The bound is uniform over all base schemes, so in particular independent of the field. The universal-quotient property of [lem-sfb-free-quotient-grassmann-projective] now gives a morphism $j_m:H\to G_k(N_m,P(m))$, where $N_m=\dim_k V_m$.

source.place: Morrison, Section 2.1, printed pp.4--5; agent expansion of the Hilbert embedding and arbitrary-characteristic central descent.

proof.text: The degree-$m$ kernel determines the whole closed family, not merely its geometric fibres. Indeed [lem-sfb-hilbert-uniform-section-bound] says that $\mathcal I$ is generated by $I_b\otimes\mathcal O(-b)$ and that multiplication $V_{m-b}\otimes I_b\to I_m$ is onto. On the projective chart $D_+(x_i)$, each local degree-$b$ generator $u$ equals $(x_i^{m-b}u)/x_i^m$ after trivializing the twists. The numerator belongs to $I_m$. Thus the image of $I_m\otimes\mathcal O(-m)$ is precisely $\mathcal I$. This calculation holds on arbitrary test schemes, including nonreduced ones. Two $T$-points of $H$ inducing the same quotient of $V_m\otimes\mathcal O_T$ have the same kernel, hence the same ideal sheaf and closed subscheme. Since $H$ represents embedded subschemes, $j_m$ is a monomorphism.

source.place: Morrison, Section 2.1, printed pp.4--5; agent expansion of the Hilbert embedding and arbitrary-characteristic central descent.

proof.text: The scheme $H$ is projective, hence proper, by [lem-sfb-projective-hilbert-polynomial-representability]. Its Grassmannian target is projective by [lem-sfb-free-quotient-grassmann-projective], hence proper and in particular separated by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper]. Therefore $j_m$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated]. Together with the monomorphism of the preceding step, [lem-pc-proper-monomorphism-closed] makes $j_m$ a closed immersion. Compose with the Plücker closed immersion of [lem-sfb-free-quotient-grassmann-projective], using [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp]. When $P(m)=0$ or $N_m$, the Grassmannian is the point $\operatorname{Spec}k$, and its Plücker map is the identity to $\mathbf P^0_k$. This also covers the empty subscheme and the full projective-space polynomial.

source.place: Morrison, Section 2.1, printed pp.4--5; agent expansion of the Hilbert embedding and arbitrary-characteristic central descent.

proof.text: In the quotient convention the Plücker point of $V_m\twoheadrightarrow Q_m$ is the line quotient $\bigwedge^{P(m)}V_m\twoheadrightarrow\bigwedge^{P(m)}Q_m$. Therefore its pulled-back hyperplane line is $\Lambda_m=\det Q_m$, by the top-exterior-power definition [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power]; locally this sends $v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge v_{P(m)}$ to the wedge of their images. In rank zero the same definition gives $\det(0)=\mathcal O_H$, so no exceptional determinant convention is needed. By [lem-pc-very-ample-ample] the hyperplane pullback is ample; [lem-sc-ample-positive-tensor-power] makes $A_m=\Lambda_m^{\otimes r}$ ample as well.

source.place: Morrison, Section 2.1, printed pp.4--5; agent expansion of the Hilbert embedding and arbitrary-characteristic central descent.

proof.text: Changing coordinates acts on the Hilbert functor: an invertible matrix carries a closed family to its image under the induced automorphism of projective space. Representability of $H$ by [lem-sfb-projective-hilbert-polynomial-representability] and [lem-pc-yoneda] turns this natural transformation into a GL action morphism. Scalar matrices induce the identity automorphism on every test scheme. The fpqc quotient property in [lem-sfb-projective-matrix-central-cover], together with full faithfulness for scheme morphisms under fpqc pullback [lem-galois-fpqc-morphisms-descend], descends this action to $\operatorname{PGL}_{r,k}$. Its unit and multiplication identities descend because they are the corresponding identities on families. The degree-$m$ quotient commutes with arbitrary base change by [lem-sfb-hilbert-uniform-section-bound], hence is equivariant for the natural SL action on $V_m$. Taking the exterior power gives the action on $\Lambda_m$; its cocycle identity holds on wedges because the two composites apply the same linear maps to every factor [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power]. This is an SL linearization lifting the coordinate action.

source.place: Morrison, Section 2.1, printed pp.4--5; agent expansion of the Hilbert embedding and arbitrary-characteristic central descent.

proof.text: For an arbitrary $k$-algebra $R$ and $t\in\mu_r(R)$, the scalar $tI$ acts on degree-$m$ coordinate polynomials by $t^m$, hence on $Q_m$ by $t^m$, and on its top wedge by $t^{mP(m)}$. Thus on $A_m$ the scalar is $t^{rmP(m)}=(t^r)^{mP(m)}=1$. This is an identity over $k[t]/(t^r-1)$, not only an assertion about geometric roots. If coordinates are identified with dual vectors, both exponents acquire a minus sign and the same identity holds. The torsor identity of [lem-sfb-projective-matrix-central-cover] identifies two SL lifts of a PGL element as $g$ and $gz$ with $z\in\mu_r$. Their isomorphisms on $A_m$ are equal by this calculation. By full faithfulness in [lem-pc-fpqc-descent], the linearization isomorphism descends along $q\times\mathrm{id}_H$ to PGL. Its unit and multiplication identities descend by the same faithfulness, checked after the covers $q\times\mathrm{id}_H$ and $q\times q\times\mathrm{id}_H$. The descended isomorphism therefore defines the required line action, with the stated SL pullback.

source.place: Morrison, Section 2.1, printed pp.4--5; agent expansion of the Hilbert embedding and arbitrary-characteristic central descent.

proof.text: Fix any algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$. Invariants on powers of $A_m$ for SL equal invariants for PGL: the equality defining invariance is an equality of module maps after pullback along the fpqc cover $q\times\mathrm{id}$, and is reflected by [lem-pc-fpqc-descent]. An SL-invariant section $s$ of $\Lambda_m^{\otimes d}$ gives the PGL-invariant section $s^r$ of $A_m^{\otimes d}$ with exactly the same nonvanishing set. Conversely a PGL-invariant section of $A_m^{\otimes d}$ is an SL-invariant section of $\Lambda_m^{\otimes rd}$. Thus the semistable sets coincide. The map $\operatorname{SL}_r(\Omega)\to\operatorname{PGL}_r(\Omega)$ is onto by [lem-sfb-projective-matrix-central-cover] (equivalently rescale a matrix by an $r$th root of its inverse determinant), so the orbits in this common set coincide. Both groups have dimension $r^2-1$, and the orbit dimension formula [lem-sfb-smooth-group-orbit-geometry] consequently gives equal dimensions of their scheme-theoretic stabilizers. Closedness of the common orbit and dimension zero of the stabilizer are therefore equivalent for the two actions. This proves equality of the stable sets too.

source.place: Morrison, Section 2.1, printed pp.4--5; agent expansion of the Hilbert embedding and arbitrary-characteristic central descent.

proof.text: The common semistable locus is an open subscheme and commutes with field extension. For clarity use the PGL linearization on $A_m$. For every $d>0$, flat cohomology base change [lem-pc-flat-cohomology-separated], in degree zero on the projective separated scheme $H$, identifies sections after $K/k$ with $K\otimes_k H^0(H,A_m^{\otimes d})$. The same flat-base-change result applied to the flat algebra $k[G]$ identifies action pullbacks with the group coaction on sections. This coaction defines invariants as the kernel of $v\mapsto\rho(v)-v\otimes1$; tensoring with a field extension is exact, so invariants also commute with $K/k$. Every invariant section after extension is a finite linear combination of extended invariant sections of the same degree. If it is nonzero at a geometric point, at least one summand is nonzero there. The union of the invariant-section nonvanishing opens over $k$ therefore has exactly the defined geometric semistable points over every extension. These nonvanishing sets are the open subschemes in [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module].

source.place: Morrison, Section 2.1, printed pp.4--5; agent expansion of the Hilbert embedding and arbitrary-characteristic central descent.

proof.text: Let $s$ be a positive-degree PGL-invariant section of a power of $A_m$. The open $U_s=H_s$ is affine of finite type by [lem-sfb-projective-polarization-section-algebra], applied to $\Lambda_m$ and the section $s$ of its corresponding positive power. Over an algebraically closed extension, an orbit in $U_s$ is closed in the full semistable locus if and only if it is closed in $U_s$. Only the reverse direction needs an argument. Suppose $y$ is in its closure inside the semistable locus and choose a homogeneous invariant $t$ nonzero at $y$. Then $t$ is nonzero on the orbit as well, since its zero set is invariant and closed. If $s$ and $t$ have degrees $a,b$ in powers of $A_m$, the invariant function $s^b/t^a$ on $H_t$ is a nonzero constant $c$ on the orbit. Its value is $c$ on the orbit closure in $H_t$, so $s(y)\ne0$. Thus every such boundary point lies in $U_s$, contradicting closedness there. Stabilizers do not change on an invariant open. Hence the project's stability condition is equivalent on $U_s$ to a closed orbit there with stabilizer dimension zero.

source.place: Morrison, Section 2.1, printed pp.4--5; agent expansion of the Hilbert embedding and arbitrary-characteristic central descent.

proof.text: On $U=U_s$ let $\mathcal S\to U$ be the scheme of stabilizers, the equalizer of action and projection inside $G\times U$ with identity section $e:U\to\mathcal S$. It is of finite type, since $G$ and $U$ are of finite type and $U$ is separated. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-fibre-dimension-open] the points of $\mathcal S$ with local fibre dimension zero form an open. Pull it back along $e$. For a geometric point $\bar u$ over an algebraically closed $\Omega$, the fibre $\mathcal S_{\bar u}$ is the stabilizer $G_{\bar u}$, a group scheme of finite type over $\Omega$ whose identity $\bar e$ is an $\Omega$-rational point. Then [lem-kun-dimension-formula] gives $\dim_{\bar e}G_{\bar u}=\dim\mathcal O_{G_{\bar u},\bar e}$, which equals $\dim G_{\bar u}$ by [lem-ag-group-identity-local-dimension]; by [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change] it is also the local dimension of $\mathcal S_u$ at $e(u)$. It follows that $D=\{x:\dim G_{\bar x}>0\}$ is a closed invariant subset of $U$. By [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change], this closed subset pulls back to the same positive-dimensional-stabilizer subset under every field extension. This also explains why tangent-space dimension, which could detect nonreduced finite stabilizers, is not used.

source.place: Morrison, Section 2.1, printed pp.4--5; agent expansion of the Hilbert embedding and arbitrary-characteristic central descent.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-affine-pgl-quotient-orbit-topology] to $U=\operatorname{Spec}E$, obtaining $p:U\to Y=\operatorname{Spec}(E^G)$ and the closed subset $p(D)$. The open $W=U\setminus p^{-1}(p(D))$ consists exactly of closed orbits with stabilizer dimension zero. Indeed a geometric fibre disjoint from $D$ has all its orbits of dimension $\dim G$ by [lem-sfb-smooth-group-orbit-geometry]; none can degenerate to a smaller-dimensional boundary orbit. Its unique closed orbit from the affine quotient theorem must therefore be the whole fibre. Conversely, if a fibre contains a closed orbit of dimension $\dim G$, any other orbit would have that orbit in its boundary and therefore larger dimension, impossible. Thus that fibre is a single orbit, is disjoint from $D$, and lies in $W$. The affine quotient and the image of $D$ commute with field extension by [lem-sfb-affine-pgl-quotient-orbit-topology]; the preceding step gives the same fact for $D$. Hence $W$ commutes with field extension. By the preceding comparison on invariant affine opens, the union of these $W$ over all $s$ is precisely the stable open in $H$. Its formation commutes with field extension: the extended invariant opens from the previous semistable-base-change step cover every extended semistable locus. The SL stable and semistable opens are the same opens, by step 7. All calculations used the full central group scheme and full stabilizers, so they also apply when $\mu_r$ is nonreduced.

(3) Projective implies proper, then proper-to-separated, then a proper monomorphism is a closed immersion, then composition with Plücker; ranks 0 and N are covered by G=S. (4) Plücker gives the wedge, so the hyperplane line is det Q_m, ample by the very-ample node and the positive-power node. (5) Full Yoneda gives the GL action, descended along GL→PGL by the one-member fpqc morphism descent.
